content: For GitLab BV (Belgium) employees with 6+ months tenure, maternity leave is paid at 100% salary for up to 16 weeks [1].

messages.content:
You answer questions about the GitLab company handbook using ONLY the numbered passages provided.
- Base every statement on the passages and cite them like [1] or [2][3].
- If the passages do not contain the answer, reply exactly: "I don't know based on the handbook." Do not guess or use outside knowledge.
- If the answer depends on a country, entity or situation, say which one the passage covers.
- Be concise: at most 3 sentences.

Passages:
[1] [GitLab BV (Belgium) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Time Off & Leave Benefits > Parental Leave]
Maternity Leave Details

**Maternity Leave**

- 15 weeks total (6 prenatal, 9 postnatal)
- For team members with 6+ months tenure: 100% salary for up to 16 weeks
- Runs concurrently with [GitLab Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave)
- Request via Workday 3 months before start date

Paternity/Co-Parent Leave Details

**Paternity/Co-Parent Leave**

- 20 days leave (15 days for births before January 1, 2023)
- Use within 4 months of birth
- 100% salary for up to 16 weeks (minus statutory entitlements)
- Runs concurrently with [GitLab's 16-week Parental Leave policy](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave)
- GitLab tops up mutual insurance fund payments to 100% salary

[2] [GitLab BV (Netherlands) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Time Off Policies > Sick Leave Support]
Comprehensive coverage when you're unable to work due to illness.

Leave Entitlement

* 100% salary for first 25 days
* 70% salary continuation for up to 104 weeks total
* GitLab complies with [Dutch local laws](https://business.gov.nl/regulation/reporting-employee-illness-recovery/) regarding sick leave. Local laws override any leave policy we have in the benefit of the team members

How to Report

* Select "Out Sick" in Workday

Employees of GitLab B.V. have further rights and responsibilities regarding sick time based on Dutch law, as written into their employment [contracts](https://internal.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/people-operations/people-operations/employment_contracts/):

[3] [GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family leaves > Maternity Leave]
Leave Entitlement

- Team members must have continuous employment with GitLab for at least 26 weeks leading up to the "qualifying week" (15th week before the expected week of childbirth)
- Up to 52 weeks leave available
- First 39 weeks paid (combining statutory and GitLab benefits)
- 90% of average earnings for first 6 weeks (before tax), then statutory rate (£194.32/week) or 90% (whichever is lower) of the team member's average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks. This also applies to the leave amounts provided for Parental Leave and Adoption Leave.
- GitLab's enhanced policy provides up to 16 weeks at 100% salary

How to Apply

[4] [GitLab BV (Netherlands) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Financial Security > Vacation Money (Vakantiegeld)]
* Statutory Sick Leave
  * Team members who are unable to work due to illness are entitled to 70% of their salary for up to 104 weeks. This leave runs concurrently with GitLab's [Sick Time Policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/). Team members will receive 100% of their salary for the first 25 days of illness.
  * GitLab complies with [Dutch local Laws](https://business.gov.nl/regulation/reporting-employee-illness-recovery/) regarding sick leave. Local laws override any leave policy we have in the benefit of the team members.
  * Team members must select `Out Sick` in Workday to ensure that all sick time is properly tracked. For complete reporting procedures, please review [the sick time procedure for The Netherlands here](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/).
* Statutory Vacation Leave
  * Team members are entitled to at least 20 vacation days per year which run concurrently with GitLab PTO. The days will accrue at 1.67 days/month from the team member's start date. Any unused days will be carried into the next calendar year, but expire on July 1st. Should the team member leave GitLab within the calendar year, an entitlement to a pro rata part vacation days exists. Team members must designate all vacation days taken as `Paid Time OFF` in Workday to ensure that vacation entitlement is properly tracked.

[5] [GitLab Ireland Ltd > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Maternity Leave]
GitLab provides comprehensive maternity leave support that goes beyond statutory requirements.  

Statutory Entitlement

- 26 weeks ordinary maternity leave  
- Additional 16 weeks unpaid leave available  
- Must start 2 weeks before due date  
- Minimum 4 weeks after birth

  

GitLab Support

- 100% salary for up to 16 weeks (includes state benefit top-up)  
- State Maternity Benefit: €262/week (subject to PRSI)  
- Support throughout your leave journey

  

How to Apply

1. Notify leaves@gitlab.com with start/end dates
2. Receive completed MB2 form from Absence Management
3. Apply via [gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/service/apply-for-maternity-benefit/) at least 6 weeks before leave
4. Submit time off in Workday (Parental Leave category)

[6] [GitLab BV (Netherlands) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Families Leaves > Statutory Partner/Paternity Leave]
Time to bond with your new child and support your partner.

Leave Entitlement

* 5 days paid Birth Leave (100% salary), to be used within 4 weeks of birth
* 5 weeks paid Additional Birth Leave within 6 months (at 70% of maximum day wage)
* Review [company policy](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave) as when more beneficial they supersede the statutory leave benefits

How to Access

1. Email [leaves@gitlab.com](mailto:leaves@gitlab.com) with your desired dates
1. Request the additional 5 weeks at least 4 weeks in advance

Question: How many weeks of maternity leave are paid at 100% salary for a GitLab BV employee with 6+ months tenure?
